D009-D008_h001.question:
I’ve been really up and down this past year. Most of the time, for about a year now, I’ve been low. I wake up feeling heavy and sad, like there’s no point to anything. Things I used to enjoy on the farm—walking the fields, working on the tractor, even sitting with my grandkids—don’t give me any pleasure anymore. Just thinking about what needs to be done wears me out; my mind gets tired fast, like I can’t hold a thought. I keep thinking it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up, or that my family would be better off without me, but I haven’t made any plans or tried anything.

Then about a month back I had this spell where I suddenly felt almost too good. My mood would flip fast—I’d be joking and on top of the world one minute, then snapping at my wife over nothing the next. I barely slept, maybe three hours a night, but I still felt wired and full of energy. I couldn’t sit still—pacing around the house, wringing my hands, starting little jobs and not finishing them. My talking got so fast my wife said she couldn’t keep up or get a word in. I was still able to manage the farm, didn’t need to go to the hospital, and I wasn’t seeing or hearing things that weren’t there.
D009-D008_h001.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D009-D008_h002.question:
For about a year now, I’ve been in this really deep low. Most days I wake up already feeling weighed down, like I’m dragging myself through mud. I used to be proud of my teaching career, the students I helped, but now even when old pupils write to thank me, I just…feel nothing. I’ve stopped going to church choir, barely see friends. Just taking a shower or fixing a simple meal feels exhausting.  

I have these thoughts a lot, like, “What’s the point of going on?” Sometimes I think it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up, though I haven’t made any plans or anything like that. It scares my husband, but I’ve never felt out of control or like I’d hurt anyone else.  

Then there are these strange “up” times, like last month, where for a few weeks I was buzzing. I’d be cheerful one minute, snapping at my husband the next. I started reorganizing the whole house, three projects at once, pacing around, wringing my hands if I tried to sit still. I talked his ear off, barely slept for several nights but felt like I didn’t need it and just kept going. I was still managing at home, though—no hospital or anything like that, and I never saw or heard things that weren’t there.
D009-D008_h002.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D009-D008_h003.question:
It’s been a really up‑and‑down couple of years. For about a year now I’ve been in this long slump. I’m exhausted all the time; just getting ready for work feels like climbing a hill. I catch myself thinking it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up, but I don’t have any plans to hurt myself.

I needed only three or four hours of sleep and woke up buzzing, full of ideas for the branch, reorganizing everything, calling clients constantly. I was talking nonstop in meetings, more social than I’ve ever been—drinks after work, networking events, reconnecting with old colleagues. It didn’t get me into serious trouble; I still did my job and was never out of control or unsafe, and I didn’t feel paranoid or hear things or anything like that.

    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

I’ve stopped meeting friends for drinks, stopped answering texts. Even simple stuff like cataloging a box of files feels exhausting; my brain just wears out so fast. 

Every now and then, though, it flips. A few months ago I had about a month where I was… weirdly great. I was buzzing, walking fast, talking nonstop at work about reorganizing the whole collection. I barely slept, maybe three hours a night, and didn’t even feel tired. I couldn’t sit still, had to keep doing something—relabeling, rearranging, starting side projects. My sex drive went through the roof; I was constantly on dating apps, hooking up more than I usually would. I was more “too intense” than actually in danger—no cops, no hospital, nothing like that, and I wasn’t seeing or hearing things.

A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D009-D008_h022.question:
For the past year or so, I’ve felt like I’m on a roller coaster. The “up” parts started about three months ago. I’d wake up feeling insanely energized and upbeat for no real reason, like I was on top of the world. I’d take on extra clients, redesign the whole gym schedule, start new training plans, and sign up for projects all at once. I barely slept—maybe a couple of hours a night—but I didn’t feel tired and didn’t think it was a problem. I was just “on,” talking fast, moving nonstop, but I was still able to do my job and didn’t do anything dangerous or out of control. I never felt out of touch with reality or heard or saw things.

Then I crash. For the last year, these down phases have been more common. I lose all drive—can’t push myself to train, cancel sessions, avoid answering texts. I pace around my apartment, can’t sit still, pick at my fingers, but can’t focus on anything. Even simple stuff like planning a workout feels mentally exhausting. Emotionally, it’s like someone turned the volume down on everything—I don’t really feel happy, sad, nothing. It’s starting to mess with my work and income.
D009-D008_h022.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder

D009-D008_h023.question:
I’ve been all over the place this past year. For a long stretch, maybe a little over a year, it’s like I’ve been running on empty. I move slow, even at work—my partner jokes I’m walking through molasses. Just getting dressed for shift change feels like a chore. I used to be proud of my case clearances, commendations, all that; now when the captain praises me, it barely registers. It’s like I’m watching my own life from behind thick glass—my emotions feel flat, even with my wife and kid. I come home exhausted and just sit there, no energy to play or talk.

Then about three months ago, things flipped. I started getting these stretches where I’m suddenly buzzing—cracking jokes, talking fast, jumping between three or four case files at once, volunteering for extra surveillance, reorganizing the whole board. My mood can swing in the same day from feeling on top of the world to snapping at colleagues over nothing. I’ll go two, three nights with barely any sleep, but I don’t feel tired, so I just keep working or cleaning the house. I’m still functioning—no one’s had to pull me off duty or send me to the hospital—and I’m not seeing or hearing things or anything like that.
D009-D008_h023.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder

D009-D008_h024.question:
It’s been a rough year. For about a year now I’ve just felt…flat and low most of the time. I used to love trying new recipes and chatting with regulars, but lately I just don’t care. My husband will ask me something and I kind of pause and search for words; even my talking feels slowed down. I’m tired all the time, even if I sleep a full night, and everything feels like wading through mud. I still open the restaurant, but it takes a lot out of me and I’ve cut back on things I used to enjoy there.

Before this long low stretch, there was about three months where I was the opposite. I was on edge and snapping at staff and my kids over tiny things. I was buzzing with energy, taking on new menu ideas, rearranging the whole place, starting several projects at once. I’d sleep maybe three or four hours a night and still wake up feeling wired and ready to go. I was definitely more intense than usual, but I didn’t lose control, need to be hospitalized, or see or hear things that weren’t there.
D009-D008_h024.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder

D009-D008_h025.question:
It’s been a strange couple of years. For about a year now I’ve mostly just felt worn down and low. I used to be up before sunrise, moving around the fields, but these days I just sit at the table staring at my coffee, trying to get myself to move. Even walking across the yard feels like I’m dragging my feet through mud. My wife says I shuffle now instead of walking. I’m tired all the time, even if I sleep a full night. I feel this steady heaviness, like a cloud that doesn’t lift, and I’ve been letting a lot of work slide because I just can’t get myself to start.

But before this long low spell, there was about three months where I was the complete opposite. I was all over the place—one minute joking and feeling on top of the world, the next snapping at my wife over nothing. I couldn’t sit still; I was constantly fixing things, starting new projects, never stopping. I’d get by on just a few hours of sleep and still wake up feeling wired, not tired. I was busy and restless, but I wasn’t out of control, didn’t need to go to the hospital, and I wasn’t seeing or hearing things.
D009-D008_h025.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder
